ck3_decoder_rules.hanzi_hex_escape: _([0-9A-F]{4}) within CJK Unified/ExtA/Compat (U+3400..U+9FFF, U+F900..U+FAFF) extracted BEFORE accent substitution
ck3_decoder_rules.scandinavian_a_ring: A__<lowercase> -> Å/å (A__sta -> Åsta, HA__kon -> Håkon, A__sa -> Åsa)
ck3_decoder_rules.lowercase_underscore_rule: Lowercase _ separates words (<word>_<Cap> -> space), Arabic inner 'ayn/hamza (-> '), or Korean/African syllables (-> -); NEVER accented.

chancellery_adaptation_laws.circumflex_purity: All long/stressed vowels strictly use â, ê, î, ô, û; acute accents á, é, í, ó, ú and carons/cedillas/barred-l are converted.
chancellery_adaptation_laws.affricates: Initial [ts] written z-; medial/final [ts] written -tz-/-tz; [tʃ] written tsch; [dʒ] written dsch.
chancellery_adaptation_laws.sinosphere_transcription: 12th-century Song/EMK/EMJ phonotactics: Pinyin zh -> dsch, q -> tsch, sh -> sch, initial c -> z; Japanese ts -> z-/-tz-, sh -> sch, j -> dsch.

Adalbero.notes: OHG adal ('noble') + bero ('bear'). Stressed open vowels lengthened with circumflex Â- and -ê-.

Adalbert.notes: OHG adal ('noble') + berht ('bright'). Open initial Â- lengthened; Rhine Franconian unshifted -b-.

Adalgod.notes: OHG adal ('noble') + Gaut ('Geat/Goth'). Final -d devoices to -t via Auslautverhärtung.

Adam.notes: Biblical Hebrew ('earth/man'). Stressed open vowel lengthened to Â-.

Ademar.notes: Old Catalan/Occitan Ademar (OHG Audamar 'wealth-famous'). Imperial house name; oxytone stress, attested with acute in imperial annals.

Adolf.notes: OHG adal ('noble') + wolf ('wolf'). Stressed initial open Â- lengthened.

Alarich.notes: Gothic/OHG All-rich ('ruler of all'). Final -ric shifted to -rîch with long î.

Alberich.notes: OHG alb ('elf') + rīhhi ('ruler'). Post-vocalic -k shifted to -ch; long -îch.

Albrecht.notes: Contracted variant of Adalbert. Stressed open Â- lengthened.

Amadeus.notes: Latin Amadeus ('love God'). Romance/Latin final -us reduced to Tarraconian schwa -êe per Rule 2.

Amalrich.notes: Gothic/Amal royal stem + rīhhi ('mighty ruler'). Suffix -rîch with long î.

Andreas.notes: Greek Andreas ('manly'). Penultimate vowel lengthened to -ê- under stress.

Anno.notes: Short hypocoristic of Arn- / Arnold. Stressed open Â- lengthened.

Anselm.notes: OHG Ans ('god') + helm ('helmet'). Standard Franconian compound.

Ansgar.notes: OHG Ans ('god') + gēr ('spear'). Stressed heavy suffix -gâr.

Arnold.notes: OHG arn ('eagle') + wald ('ruler'). Auslautverhärtung -d -> -t; corresponds to Catalan Arnau.

Arnulf.notes: OHG arn ('eagle') + wolf ('wolf'). Dynastic saint of Metz; Franconian/Romance vowel rounding -olf.

Augustin.notes: Latin Augustinus ('venerable'). Stressed final long -în per Rule 2/6.

Baldarich.notes: OHG bald ('bold') + rīhhi ('ruler'). Open Â- and -rîch.

Baldomar.notes: OHG bald ('bold') + māri ('famous'). Double circumflex on stressed bimoraic roots.

Baldur.notes: Old Norse/Germanic Baldr ('lord/prince'). Initial Â- lengthened.

Berengar.notes: Catalan/Occitan Berenguer (OHG Beringar). Heavy final stress -gâr.

Bernhard.notes: OHG bern ('bear') + hard ('brave'). Auslautverhärtung -d -> -t; Catalan Bernat.

Bruno.notes: OHG brūn ('brown/shining'). Preserved MHG unshifted long û.

Burchard.notes: OHG burg ('fortress') + hard ('strong'). Shifted post-vocalic -ch- and Auslautverhärtung -t.

Christopher.notes: Greek Christophoros ('Christ-bearer'). Apocopated final syllable per Rule 2; initial Ch-.

Dieter.notes: Hypocoristic of Dietrich. Preserved unshifted Franconian D-; long î.

Dietmar.notes: OHG thiot ('people') + māri ('famous'). Preserved D-; long î.

Dietpold.notes: OHG thiot ('people') + bald ('bold'). Franconian D-; Auslautverhärtung -t.

Dietrich.notes: OHG thiot ('people') + rīhhi ('ruler'). Classical Franconian D- and -rîch.

Dietwin.notes: OHG thiot ('people') + wīn ('friend'). Preserved D- and long -wîn.

Drogo.notes: Old Franconian name of Carolingian princes; lenition of medial -g- [ɣ]; long Ô-.

Eberhard.notes: OHG ebur ('boar') + hard ('brave'). Stressed initial open Ê-; Auslautverhärtung -t.

Eginolf.notes: OHG egin ('blade/edge') + wolf ('wolf'). Initial Ê- lengthened; rounded -olf.

Ehrenfried.notes: OHG ēra ('honor') + fridu ('peace'). Initial Ê-; long unshifted -frît.

Emich.notes: Franconian hypocoristic of Emmerich. Vowels lengthened under bimoraic constraint.

Emmerich.notes: OHG Amalrich ('ruler of work'). Shifted suffix -rîch.

Engelbert.notes: OHG Angil ('Angle/angel') + berht ('bright'). Standard Franconian form.

Erich.notes: Old Norse Eiríkr / OHG Era-rīhhi ('sole ruler'). Initial Ê-; long -rîch.

Ezzo.notes: Franconian hypocoristic (count palatine of Lotharingia). Medial affricate -tz- per Rule 2.2/5.

Farabert.notes: OHG fara ('lineage/travel') + berht ('bright'). Initial open Fâ-.

Filibert.notes: OHG filu ('much') + berht ('bright'). Open initial Fî- lengthened.

Folmar.notes: Contracted variant of Folkmar (counts of Blieskastel/Metz).

Franz.notes: OHG/Romance Franciscus ('Frankish/free'). Affricate strictly written -tz per Rule 2.2.

Friedrich.notes: OHG fridu ('peace') + rīhhi ('ruler'). Preserved MHG unshifted long î; -rîch.

GU_nther.notes: OHG gund ('battle') + heri ('army'). Umlauted close front rounded ü; interdental th -> t.

Gautselin.notes: Old Catalan/Occitan Gaucelm / OHG Gautila. Medial affricate -tz-; long suffix -în.

Georg.notes: Patron knight of Catalonia (Sant Jordi); Chancellery form Dschôrdi or German Jôrch / Georg [ˈɡeː.ɔrx].

Gerhard.notes: OHG gēr ('spear') + hard ('brave'). Auslautverhärtung -d -> -t; Catalan Guerau.

Gerlach.notes: OHG gēr ('spear') + leih ('play/dance'). Long initial Gêr-.

Giselbert.notes: OHG gīsal ('pledge/hostage') + berht ('bright'). Duke of Lotharingia; long Gî-.

Gottfried.notes: OHG got ('God') + fridu ('peace'). Cluster simplification and Auslautverhärtung -frît; Catalan Jofre.

Gottschalk.notes: OHG got ('God') + scale ('servant'). Classical Franconian orthography.

Gotzelo.notes: Lothringian ducal hypocoristic of Gottfried. Medial affricate -tz-; long Ô-.

Guntram.notes: OHG gund ('battle') + hraban ('raven'). Attested Chatenois dynastic name; closed syllable.

Gunzelin.notes: Hypocoristic of Gunther/Guntram. Medial affricate -tz-; suffix -în.

Hans.notes: Hypocoristic of Johannes. Vowel lengthened before -ns coda.

Hartwig.notes: OHG hard ('brave') + wīg ('battle'). Final -g devoices to -ch via Auslautverhärtung.

Hatto.notes: Franconian hypocoristic of Hadu- ('battle'). Open initial Hâ-.

Heinrich.notes: OHG heim ('home') + rīhhi ('ruler'). Rhine-Moselle Franconian Heimrîch / Hênrîch; -rîch.

Heribert.notes: OHG heri ('army') + berht ('bright'). Open vowels lengthened Hêrî-.

Hermann.notes: OHG heri ('army') + man ('man'). Standard Germanic compound.

Hesso.notes: Franconian/Hessian hypocoristic. Long vowel before geminate.

Hoger.notes: OHG hōh ('high') + gēr ('spear'). Lenited medial -g- [ɣ]; long Hô-.

Hugo.notes: OHG hugu ('mind/spirit'). Preserved long û; lenited medial -g- [ɣ]; Catalan Hug.

Humbert.notes: OHG hūn ('bear cub/giant') + berht ('bright'). Standard Franconian form.

Hupold.notes: OHG hugu ('mind') + bald ('bold'). Auslautverhärtung -d -> -t; long Hû-.

JU_rgen.notes: Low German/Franconian variant of Georg. Medial lenited -g- [ɣ].

Johann.notes: Hebrew Yohanan ('God is gracious'). Imperial chancellery form Johann / Jôhân.

Karl.notes: OHG karl ('free man'). Lengthened before liquid coda cluster -rl.

Konrad.notes: OHG kuoni ('bold') + rāt ('counsel'). Imperial Latin-Franconian Cônrât / Konrat; -d -> -t.

Kuno.notes: Hypocoristic of Konrad. Preserved long û.

Lambert.notes: OHG land ('land') + berht ('bright'). Patron of Maastricht/Liège; Franconian unshifted -p-.

Landolf.notes: OHG land ('land') + wolf ('wolf'). Standard Franconian compound.

Leopold.notes: OHG liut ('people') + bald ('bold'). Franconian contracted Lîpolt / Lîopold; -t.

Liudolf.notes: OHG liut ('people') + wolf ('wolf'). Saxon/Franconian royal stem.

Liutbert.notes: OHG liut ('people') + berht ('bright'). Preserved diphthong iu.

Liutpold.notes: OHG liut ('people') + bald ('bold'). Attested Chatenois name; Auslautverhärtung -t.

Lothar.notes: OHG hluod ('fame') + heri ('army'). Eponym of Lotharingia; double circumflex Lôthâr.

Ludolf.notes: Variant of Liudolf with monophthongized long û.

Ludwig.notes: OHG hluod ('fame') + wīg ('battle'). Auslautverhärtung -g -> -ch; Rhine-Franconian Lôdewîch / Lûdewîch.

Lutbert.notes: OHG liut ('people') + berht ('bright'). Upper Franconian unshifted -p-.

Magnus.notes: Latin Magnus ('great'). Imperial court title adopted as given name.

Martin.notes: Latin Martinus ('of Mars'). Patron of the Franks; stressed final long -în.

Matthias.notes: Hebrew Mattityahu ('gift of God'). Penultimate vowel lengthened.

Meginher.notes: OHG magan ('strength') + heri ('army'). Long initial Mê-.

Michael.notes: Hebrew Mikha'el ('who is like God?'). Archangel, patron of the Empire; -ch-.

Milo.notes: Old Frankish/Romance hypocoristic. Preserved long Î-.

Nikolaus.notes: Greek Nikolaos ('victory of the people'). Patron of Lotharingia; long vowels Nîkôlôs / Niklâs.

Norbert.notes: OHG nord ('north') + berht ('bright'). Founder of Premonstratensians (Xanten/Lorraine).

Otbert.notes: OHG ōd ('wealth') + berht ('bright'). Open initial Ô-; unshifted -p-.

Otto.notes: OHG ōd ('wealth'). Imperial Saxon/Franconian name; open initial Ô- lengthened.

Peter.notes: Greek Petros ('rock'). Prince of the Apostles; Franconian unshifted P-; long Pê- (Catalan Pere).

Philipp.notes: Greek Philippos ('horse lover'). Royal Capetian/Imperial name; long vowels Phîlîpp.

Poppo.notes: Franconian/Babenberg hypocoristic. Rhine Franconian unshifted P-; long Pô-.

Radbot.notes: OHG rāt ('counsel') + bodo ('messenger'). Auslautverhärtung -d -> -t; long vowels Râtbôt.

Reginar.notes: OHG ragin ('counsel') + heri ('army'). Ancestral dynasty of Lotharingia (House of Reginar).

Rudolf.notes: OHG hruod ('fame') + wolf ('wolf'). West Franconian Rôdolf / Rûdolf.

Ruprecht.notes: OHG hruod ('fame') + berht ('bright'). Palatine Franconian Rôprecht.

Rutger.notes: OHG hruod ('fame') + gēr ('spear'). Preserved dental stop -t-; long Rôt-.

Siegfried.notes: OHG sigu ('victory') + fridu ('peace'). Unshifted MHG long î; devoiced -c- and -frît.

Sieghard.notes: OHG sigu ('victory') + hard ('brave'). Attested Chatenois dynastic name; Auslautverhärtung -t.

Simon.notes: Hebrew Shim'on ('he has heard'). Stressed long vowels Sîmôn.

Stefan.notes: Greek Stephanos ('crown'). Protomartyr; Franconian geminate ff; Catalan Esteve.

Tagino.notes: OHG tag ('day'). Lengthened open Tâ-; suffix -în.

Thachulf.notes: OHG daha ('clay/tough') + wolf ('wolf'). Franconian unshifted D-; -ch-.

Thankulf.notes: OHG thank ('thought/gratitude') + wolf ('wolf'). Franconian D-; rounded -olf.

Thietmar.notes: OHG thiot ('people') + māri ('famous'). Classical Franconian Dîtmar with long î.

Thomas.notes: Aramaic Te'oma ('twin'). Stressed double circumflex Thômâs.

Udalrich.notes: OHG uodal ('heritage') + rīhhi ('ruler'). Long U- and -rîch.

Ulrich.notes: Contracted variant of Udalrich. Shifted suffix -rîch.

Viktor.notes: Latin Victor ('conqueror'). Romance loan with labiodental V- [v]; long -tôr.

Waldemar.notes: Slavic Vladimir / Germanic Waldemar ('fame-ruler'). Double circumflex Wâldemâr.

Walram.notes: OHG walah ('foreigner/Romance') + hraban ('raven'). Counts of Arlon/Limburg.

Walther.notes: OHG wald ('rule') + heri ('army'). High German epic hero (Walther von Aquitanien).

Welf.notes: Germanic Welf ('whelp/wolf cub'). Dynastic royal stem.

Wenzel.notes: Slavic Václav / MHG Wenzel. Affricate strictly written -tz- per Rule 2.2.

Werner.notes: OHG warin ('guard') + heri ('army'). Standard Franconian form.

Wernhard.notes: OHG warin ('guard') + hard ('brave'). Name of Augustus Wernhard 'the Bear'; -d -> -t in speech, written -hard in imperial charter.

Wido.notes: OHG witu ('wood/forest'). French Guy / Italian Guido; long Wî-.

Wigerich.notes: OHG wīg ('battle') + rīhhi ('ruler'). Count palatine of Lotharingia; long Wî- and -rîch.

Wilbert.notes: OHG willio ('will') + berht ('bright'). Standard Franconian form.

Wilhelm.notes: OHG willio ('will') + helm ('helmet'). Corresponds to Catalan Guilhem.

Wolfgang.notes: OHG wolf ('wolf') + gang ('stride/path'). Saint bishop of Regensburg.

Wolfram.notes: OHG wolf ('wolf') + hraban ('raven'). Chivalric epic poet name.

Adela.notes: OHG adal ('noble'). Stressed open Â- lengthened; final -a reduced to High German schwa -e.

Adelheid.notes: OHG adal ('noble') + heit ('kind/state'). Auslautverhärtung -d -> -t; corresponds to French/Catalan Adélaïde / Azalaïs.

Agathe.notes: Greek Agathe ('good'). Open initial Â- lengthened.

Agnes.notes: Greek Hagne ('pure'). Stressed oxytone -ês; Occitan/Catalan Anjês [a.ˈɲeːs].

Alberade.notes: OHG alb ('elf') + rāt ('counsel'). Stressed open -râde lengthened.

Amalberga.notes: Gothic/Amal stem + berg ('protection'). Final -a reduced to schwa -e.

Amalie.notes: Gothic Amal ('work/vigor'). Open -mâ- lengthened under stress.

Barbara.notes: Greek Barbara ('foreign'). Final unstressed -a reduced to schwa -e per Rule 2.

Beatrix.notes: Latin Beatrix ('she who blesses'). Stressed long -trîx; Catalan Bêatrîs.

Berchte.notes: OHG berht ('bright'). Pre-Christian light goddess / Franconian name; -ch-.

Berta.notes: OHG berht ('bright'). Carolingian queen name; final -a reduced to schwa -e.

Brunhilde.notes: OHG brūna ('armor/brown') + hiltia ('battle'). Preserved long û; Auslautverhärtung -d -> -t.

Cecilie.notes: Latin Caecilia ('blind'). Initial affricate C- [ts]; long -cî-.

Christine.notes: Greek Christiane ('follower of Christ'). Initial Ch- [k]; long vowels Chrîstîne.

Cothilda.notes: Frankish royal Chrodechildis ('famous battle'). Long Chô-; Auslautverhärtung -t.

Dorothea.notes: Greek Dorothea ('gift of God'). Final -ea reduced to -êe per Rule 2/102.

Elisabeth.notes: Hebrew Elisheva ('God is my oath'). Penultimate long -lî-; final -t.

Emma.notes: OHG Ermen ('whole/universal'). Final -a reduced to schwa -e per Rule 2.

Engeltraud.notes: OHG angil ('angel') + trūd ('strength/beloved'). Lenited -drût with long û.

Ermengard.notes: OHG ermen ('universal') + gard ('enclosure/protection'). Auslautverhärtung -d -> -t; Catalan Ermengarda.

Eufemia.notes: Greek Euphemia ('auspicious speech'). Suffix -eia/-ia -> -êmîe per Rule 2.

Frida.notes: OHG fridu ('peace'). Preserved MHG long î; final schwa -e.

Friedrica.notes: Feminine of Friedrich. Shifted suffix -rîche with long î.

Gerberga.notes: OHG gēr ('spear') + berg ('protection'). Carolingian/Ottonian queen name; final -e.

Gertrude.notes: OHG gēr ('spear') + trūd ('strength'). Franconian lenition to -drût with long unshifted û.

Gisela.notes: OHG gīsal ('pledge'). Open initial Gî- lengthened; final -e.

Gudrun.notes: Old Norse/Germanic Guðrún ('battle-rune'). Stressed heavy suffix -rûn.

Hedwig.notes: OHG hadu ('battle') + wīg ('fight'). Stressed Hêd-; final -g devoices to -ch.

Heike.notes: Low Franconian hypocoristic of Heinrich. Falling diphthong ei.

Helene.notes: Greek Helene ('torch/light'). Stressed long -lê-; mother of Constantine.

Helga.notes: Old Norse Heilagr ('holy'). Final -a reduced to schwa -e.

Hemma.notes: Franconian royal queen name (wife of Louis the German). Final -e.

Henrike.notes: Feminine of Heinrich. Franconian Heimrîche with shifted -rîche.

Heylwig.notes: OHG heilig ('holy') + wīg ('battle'). Final -g devoices to -ch.

Hildeburg.notes: OHG hiltia ('battle') + burg ('stronghold'). Final -g shifts to velar fricative -ch per Rule 1.3.

Hildegard.notes: OHG hiltia ('battle') + gard ('protection'). Auslautverhärtung -d -> -t; Saint Hildegard.

Ida.notes: OHG īda ('work/industrious'). Preserved long Î-; final -e.

Ilsa.notes: Hypocoristic of Elisabeth. Lengthened Î- before -ls- cluster; final -e.

Inga.notes: Germanic Yngvi (divine ancestor). Final -a reduced to schwa -e.

Ingeltrude.notes: OHG Ingel + trūd ('strength'). Franconian lenition to -drût with long û.

Irmele.notes: Franconian diminutive of Irmgard/Irmina. Standard schwa ending.

Irmeltrud.notes: OHG ermen ('universal') + trūd ('strength'). Lenition to -drût with long û.

Isentrude.notes: OHG īsan ('iron') + trūd ('strength'). Long Î- and -drût.

Jutta.notes: Hypocoristic of Judith. Stressed open Jû- lengthened; final -e.

Karlotte.notes: Romance diminutive of Karl. Stressed Kârl-.

Katharina.notes: Greek Aikaterine ('pure'). High medieval standard Katrîne with long -rîne.

Klara.notes: Latin Clara ('bright/clear'). Open Clâ- lengthened; final -a reduced to schwa -e.

Konstanze.notes: Latin Constantia ('constancy'). Affricate written -tz- per Rule 2.2; long -stân-.

Kriemhild.notes: OHG Grīm-hilt ('masked battle'). Initial Ch-; Auslautverhärtung -t.

Kunigunde.notes: OHG kuoni ('bold') + gund ('battle'). Imperial empress-saint; long Kû-; -d -> -t.

Margarete.notes: Greek Margarites ('pearl'). Stressed -re- lengthened; variant Margarîte.

Maria.notes: Hebrew Miryam ('rebellion/beloved'). Mother of God; final -ia -> -îe per Rule 2.

Oda.notes: OHG ōd ('wealth'). Stressed open Ô- lengthened; final -e.

Richara.notes: OHG rīhhi ('powerful/noble') + heri ('army'). Long Rîch-; final -e.

Richenza.notes: OHG rīhhi ('mighty'). Affricate strictly written -tz- per Rule 2.2; long Rîch-.

Richwara.notes: OHG rīhhi ('noble') + war ('guardian'). Long Rîch-; final -e.

Romilda.notes: OHG hruom ('fame') + hiltia ('battle'). Stressed Rôm-; Auslautverhärtung -t.

Serhilda.notes: OHG sarwo ('armor') + hiltia ('battle'). Stressed Sêr-; Auslautverhärtung -t.

Sofie.notes: Greek Sophia ('wisdom'). Stressed double long Sôphîe.

Trude.notes: Hypocoristic of Gertrude/Irmtrud. Franconian D-; long û; final -e.

Ulrike.notes: Feminine of Ulrich. Shifted suffix -rîche with long î.

Ursula.notes: Latin Ursula ('little she-bear'). Patron of Cologne; stressed long Û-; final -e.

Ute.notes: OHG uodal ('heritage'). Heroine of the Nibelungenlied; long Û-; final -e.

Walpurga.notes: OHG wald ('rule') + burg ('protection'). Final -g shifts to velar fricative -ch per Rule 1.3.

Wilhelmina.notes: Feminine of Wilhelm. Suffix -îne with long î; final -e.

Wiltrud.notes: OHG willio ('will') + trūd ('strength'). Double long Wîltrût; -d -> -t.

fructuôs.notes: Bishop of Tarragona, patron of Tarraco amphitheater.

vintzent.notes: Deacon martyr of Saragossa, premier martyr of Hispania.

dschôrdi.notes: Sant Jordi / St. George, patron knight of Catalonia.

feliu.notes: Sant Feliu / Felix of Girona, deacon martyr.

nartzîs.notes: Sant Narcís / Narcissus of Girona & Augsburg.

brâuli.notes: San Braulio, bishop of Saragossa & scholar.

îsidôr.notes: San Isidoro of Seville, Doctor of the Church.

leânt.notes: San Leandro of Seville, converter of Visigoths.

ermengilt.notes: San Hermenegildo, Catholic prince martyred in Tarragona.

prûdentz.notes: Aurelius Prudentius, Christian Latin poet of Tarraconensis.

chrôdegang.notes: Bishop of Metz, liturgical reformer of Frankish empire.

gôerîch.notes: Bishop of Metz, successor to Arnulf.

klêmens.notes: First apostle and bishop of Metz; dragon slayer.

hûprecht.notes: St. Hubert of Liège, apostle of Ardennes & hunters.

willibrort.notes: Apostle of Frisia, founder of Echternach (Luxembourg).

kîljan.notes: St. Kilian of Würzburg, Apostle of Franconia.

bônifâtz.notes: St. Boniface of Mainz, Apostle of Germany.

gêrêon.notes: St. Gereon of Cologne, Theban Legion martyr.

môrîtz.notes: St. Maurice, leader of Theban Legion & HRE patron.

laurenz.notes: St. Laurence of Osca/Rome, archdeacon martyr.

costantîn.notes: Constantine the Great, founder of Christian empire.

traiân.notes: Emperor Trajan, Optimus Princeps of Hispania.

hadriân.notes: Emperor Hadrian, builder and scholar of Hispania.

theodôsi.notes: Emperor Theodosius the Great of Cauca (Tarraconensis).

dâvît.notes: King David, psalmist and imperial model.

manuêl.notes: Manuel Komnenos, imperial diplomat and warrior.

eulâlie.notes: Santa Eulàlia, virgin martyr and patroness of Barcelona.

engrâtie.notes: Santa Engracia of Saragossa, celebrated by Prudentius.

juste.notes: Santa Justa of Seville, virgin potter martyr.

rûfîne.notes: Santa Rufina of Seville, virgin potter martyr.

montserrât.notes: Our Lady of Montserrat, holy saw-mountain of Catalonia.

pîlâr.notes: Our Lady of the Pillar in Saragossa, oldest Marian shrine.

assumpziôn.notes: The Assumption of Our Lady, patronal feast of Tarragona.

stelle-marîs.notes: Star of the Sea, protectress of Mediterranean mariners.

nûrîe.notes: Our Lady of Núria, Pyrenean Marian sanctuary in Ripoll.

mercêt.notes: Our Lady of Mercy, protectress of captives and fleet.

irmîne.notes: St. Irmina of Oeren, co-founder of Echternach Abbey.

begge.notes: St. Begga of Landen, Carolingian matriarch of Andenne.

glôdesînde.notes: St. Glodesind, 6th-century abbess of Sainte-Glossinde in Metz.

waldrût.notes: St. Waldetrude of Mons, patroness of Hainaut.

hêlêne.notes: Empress Helena Augusta, discoverer of True Cross, Trier palace.

katrîne.notes: St. Catherine of Alexandria, patroness of imperial chancellery.

lûtzîe.notes: St. Lucy of Syracuse, patroness of light and vision.

anasthâsîe.notes: St. Anastasia of Sirmium, celebrated at Christmas Palatine Mass.

ermessende.notes: Ermessenda of Carcassonne, legendary countess of Barcelona.

almôdis.notes: Almodis of la Marche, countess of Barcelona.

guillelme.notes: Guillema / Guilla, noble courtly name of Barcelona.

arsende.notes: Arsenda, countess of Pallars and Urgell.

doltze.notes: Dolça / Dulcia, countess of Provence and Barcelona.

santze.notes: Sança, royal infanta of Aragon and Navarre.

violant.notes: Violant / Iolanthe, royal queen consort name.

geldovîre.notes: Geldovira / Elvira, Visigothic royal infanta name.

therêse.notes: Teresa, royal infanta name of León and Castile.

theophanû.notes: Theophano, Byzantine princess and Western empress.

ânne.notes: Anna Komnene, imperial historian and princess.
